newsitem.title: JAPAN: Nuclear waste ship to arrive in Japan on March 18.
newsitem.headline: Nuclear waste ship to arrive in Japan on March 18.

text.p: A ship carrying nuclear waste from France to Japan is expected to reach a port in northern Japan on March 18, environmentalist group Greenpeace said on Wednesday.
"We don't know the current exact location of the ship, but we expect it to enter Mutsu-Ogawara Port on March 18," said Noriko Oyama of Greenpeace Japan.
The British freighter Pacific Teal left the French port of Cherbourg on January 13 carrying processed nuclear waste to a nuclear reprocessing plant in northern Japan.
Mutsu-Ogawara Port is located within the reprocessing plant complex at Rokkasho village in Aomori Prefecture, about 580 km (360 miles) northeast of Tokyo.
The ship was last observed sailing the Tasman Sea on February 25, according to Greenpeace.
Environmental and protest groups plan to camp out near the complex on March 17 to protest the arrival of the vessel the following day, Oyama said.
It is the second such shipment to Japan from France. Unlike the first shipment in 1995, the route of the shipment was made public shortly after the vessel left France.
